questions.q: The origin of campus cultism in Nigeria is historically traced back to the establishment of the **Pyrates Confraternity** in 1952 at the...
options: University of Lagos.
Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria.
University College, Ibadan.
University of Nigeria, Nsukka.
questions.explain: Campus confraternities in Nigeria began in **1952 at University College, Ibadan** (now the University of Ibadan), when Professor Wole Soyinka and six others (the "Magnificent Seven") founded the Pyrates Confraternity, also known as the National Association of Seadogs.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: When the first student confraternity was formed in Nigeria by the "Magnificent Seven", its primary and original objective was to...
options: enforce a violent monopoly over student union politics.
combat elitism, tribalism, and colonial oppression on campus.
serve as an underground militia for the university administration.
organize armed robberies to fund external student activities.
questions.explain: The **Pyrates Confraternity** was initially established as a peaceful, progressive, and patriotic organization meant to combat tribalism, elitism, and the colonial mindset among students. It was only in later decades that splinter groups deviated into the violent secret cults seen today.

questions.q: In the study of secret cults in Nigerian tertiary institutions, the **Neo Black Movement (NBM)** is commonly associated with which of the following symbols?
options: A red flying bird
A skull and crossbones
An upright black axe
A crossed anchor and rope
questions.explain:
Different cult groups are identifiable by their unique symbols, which reflect their ideologies and historical splinterings:

| Cult Group | Common Symbol |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Pyrates Confraternity** | Skull and crossbones |
| **Buccaneers (Sea Lords)** | Yellow color / Albatross |
| **Black Axe (NBM)** | Upright Black Axe |
| **Supreme Vikings** | Crossed axes and a boat |

questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary psychological reason why many youths are lured into joining secret cults on campus?
options: To secure automatic employment in the federal civil service
The desire for an intimidating status and a false sense of security
To gain exemption from the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)
The urge to voluntarily finance the university management's projects
questions.explain: Many students are lured into cultism due to peer pressure, curiosity, or the **illusion of power, popularity, and security** (protection from intimidation). Unfortunately, this false sense of security eventually exposes them to extreme danger and violence.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: A major direct consequence of cult activities on the educational system in Nigeria is the...
options: frequent disruption of the academic calendar and loss of lives.
rapid expansion of university infrastructural projects.
creation of foreign exchange revenue for tertiary institutions.
improvement in the quality of student union elections.
questions.explain: Cult-related clashes lead to violence, destruction of school property, loss of lives, and widespread insecurity, which in turn forces university authorities to close down schools, causing **frequent disruptions to the academic calendar**.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following constitutes the most effective institutional approach to eradicating cultism in tertiary institutions?
options: Encouraging students to form heavily armed campus vigilante groups
Providing financial stipends exclusively to active cult members
Imposing stiff penalties such as rustication and prosecution for convicted cultists
Promoting inter-cult rivalries during school sports festivals
questions.explain: To combat cultism effectively, university administrations and the government must enforce strict laws, ensuring that anyone caught participating in cult activities faces severe consequences, including **rustication (expulsion) and criminal prosecution**.
